compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
Each row is a fictional example. Both colleagues have the same facts, authority, procedure and deadline within that situation.

Most rows illustrate how much to settle or keep open. Either person can use the approach in either column. These are examples of the preference framework and cannot identify anyone’s type.

| Shared situation | ESTJ: possible emphasis | ESTP: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both find the same misplaced price label | Agree on a provisional plan to prevent it recurring | Keep more than one prevention plan open until the same review | J/P: provisional closure or keeping options open. Both follow the same pricing policy. |
| Both face the same staffing shortage | Set a provisional staffing plan within the same shift limits | Keep two feasible staffing plans open until the same review point | J/P: how much to settle in advance |
| Both review the same recurring issue | Compare the documented dates and circumstances of each occurrence | Compare the same dates and circumstances | Shared S: concrete information and prior experience |
| Both receive the same objection to a proposed plan | Set a provisional plan subject to review of the objection | Keep both feasible plans open until the same review | J/P: structure or openness within the same deadline |
| Both prepare the same inspection report | Agree on a provisional outline and revise it when the remaining facts arrive | Keep several workable outlines open until the same facts arrive | J/P: how much structure to give the work before review |
| Both need a schedule that meets the same new policy | Set a provisional compliant schedule | Keep more than one compliant schedule open until the same decision point | J/P: closure or flexibility. Both follow the policy. |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Imagine two managers who use the same checklist to ask that an open issue be resolved. Their training and responsibility may explain that similarity. How directly either person speaks gives little evidence about J/P.

The shared E, S and T concern attention, information and judgment, respectively. J/P concerns structure and openness in the outside world. Two colleagues can agree on what the facts show and still prefer to settle different parts of the plan.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: how much to settle during a store inspection

In a fictional store inspection, two colleagues find gaps on a display and receive the same stock and delivery records. They have the same authority and deadline to propose a follow-up. Both can check why shelves were not replenished.

The team could agree on a provisional plan and revise it after confirming the cause. Or it could keep several feasible plans open until the same review point. That contrast illustrates J/P. Either colleague could propose either approach.

A provisional plan helps people coordinate, but assumptions need to be marked. Keeping options open is useful only if someone knows when the decision will be made. Either person can check the facts and set a follow-up date.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: why their stacks differ when one letter changes

Both types have E, so the outward-facing function is dominant. In ESTJ, J points to a judging function and T identifies it as extraverted Thinking (Te), supported by introverted Sensing (Si). In ESTP, P points to a perceiving function and S identifies it as extraverted Sensing (Se), supported by introverted Thinking (Ti).

The two sets of abbreviations are different under the convention shown. Both still contain Sensing and Thinking, in different orientations and positions. A function’s place in the model does not determine when someone will take a particular step.

The Foundation lists Intuition (Ne or Ni) as the tertiary function for ESTJ and Feeling (Fe or Fi) for ESTP. This article uses Ne and Fe. Using Ni for ESTJ or Fi for ESTP would create overlap with the other type’s inferior function. See the [ESTJ profile](/en/personality/estj) and the [ESTP profile](/en/personality/estp) for their four preferences.
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
The following fictional scenes illustrate how people could make arrangements. Assign real responsibilities according to skill, authority, information and availability.

A team can agree on who will follow up and still leave the choice of remedy open. Clarify which decisions are settled and which depend on further information.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: documenting an issue found during an inspection

In a fictional store inspection, two employees find a refrigerated display outside the store’s accepted range. Both follow the same food-safety procedure and notify the responsible person. The comparison concerns the later follow-up rather than the immediate handling of the issue.

Both colleagues have the same record and deadline for a proposed follow-up. They can set a provisional review plan with an owner, or keep several follow-up options open until the authorised person assesses the findings.

They can also agree on an owner and deadline while leaving the remedy open. Either person can suggest that combination.

Record who made each observation, where the information came from and when each step took place. If a fact is missing, leave it marked as unknown. A detailed record cannot establish who visited first or what their type is.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: handling a queue during the lunch rush

In a fictional lunch rush, three delivery orders are running late. Both shift leads see the same queue and have the same staff and authority to change assignments within the store’s procedures.

One option is to set a provisional packing and handover arrangement for the rest of the rush. Another is to keep two feasible assignments available until the next check on the queue. Both approaches need clear ownership for orders already in progress.

Review what reduced the backlog and tell the next shift what changed. That evaluates the arrangement. It does not identify either shift lead’s type.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: agreeing on a relative’s temporary stay

In a fictional household, a relative asks whether their child can stay while starting university. Both household members have the same information about the proposed dates and what the home can accommodate.

Everyone affected might agree on a provisional arrangement for the whole stay or set essential terms and keep some details open for review. Neither option assumes consent from people who have not agreed.

Name what everyone needs to agree before the stay, such as the dates and access to the home. Decide what can be reviewed later, such as how chores are shared. Either person can raise both points.

compare_blocks.body:
An organised desk or careful filing can reflect habit or a requirement of the job. J/P describes a preference for structure or openness in the outside world.

Either type can speak plainly or gently. The shared Thinking preference concerns what carries weight in a judgment, so tone does not establish it.

Supervising staff and adapting to changing conditions both require skills. Neither type has exclusive claim to either skill.

Opening a follow-up record or inspecting a shelf first may reflect the assignment, deadline or information on hand. The order alone does not distinguish ESTJ from ESTP.

ESTJ and ESTP share Extraversion (E), Sensing (S) and Thinking (T). They differ only on Judging and Perceiving (J/P). ESTJ’s J favours structure and closure in the outside world. ESTP’s P favours keeping options open to new information.

- **Shared E.** Extraversion describes a preference for directing attention and energy outward. Either type can listen quietly or speak at length.
- **Shared S.** Sensing emphasises concrete details and experience when taking in information. Both can examine the same shelf and consult the same records.
- **Shared T.** Thinking emphasises logical consistency and criteria that apply across cases. Either type can use those criteria and consider how a decision affects people.
- **The J/P difference.** In type dynamics, J points to an outward-facing judging function, Te for ESTJ. P points to an outward-facing perceiving function, Se for ESTP.

Under the convention used here, ESTJ is Te–Si–Ne–Fi and ESTP is Se–Ti–Fe–Ni. Both are extraverted, so their outward functions are dominant. Their auxiliary functions face inward: Si for ESTJ and Ti for ESTP. The Myers & Briggs Foundation lists alternative orientations for the tertiary functions.

compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
Each row is a fictional example. Both colleagues have the same facts, authority, procedure and deadline within that situation.

Most rows illustrate how much to settle or keep open. Either person can use the approach in either column. These are examples of the preference framework and cannot identify anyone’s type.

| Shared situation | ESTJ: possible emphasis | ESTP: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both find the same misplaced price label | Agree on a provisional plan to prevent it recurring | Keep more than one prevention plan open until the same review | J/P: provisional closure or keeping options open. Both follow the same pricing policy. |
| Both face the same staffing shortage | Set a provisional staffing plan within the same shift limits | Keep two feasible staffing plans open until the same review point | J/P: how much to settle in advance |
| Both review the same recurring issue | Compare the documented dates and circumstances of each occurrence | Compare the same dates and circumstances | Shared S: concrete information and prior experience |
| Both receive the same objection to a proposed plan | Set a provisional plan subject to review of the objection | Keep both feasible plans open until the same review | J/P: structure or openness within the same deadline |
| Both prepare the same inspection report | Agree on a provisional outline and revise it when the remaining facts arrive | Keep several workable outlines open until the same facts arrive | J/P: how much structure to give the work before review |
| Both need a schedule that meets the same new policy | Set a provisional compliant schedule | Keep more than one compliant schedule open until the same decision point | J/P: closure or flexibility. Both follow the policy. |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Imagine two managers who use the same checklist to ask that an open issue be resolved. Their training and responsibility may explain that similarity. How directly either person speaks gives little evidence about J/P.

The shared E, S and T concern attention, information and judgment, respectively. J/P concerns structure and openness in the outside world. Two colleagues can agree on what the facts show and still prefer to settle different parts of the plan.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: how much to settle during a store inspection

In a fictional store inspection, two colleagues find gaps on a display and receive the same stock and delivery records. They have the same authority and deadline to propose a follow-up. Both can check why shelves were not replenished.

The team could agree on a provisional plan and revise it after confirming the cause. Or it could keep several feasible plans open until the same review point. That contrast illustrates J/P. Either colleague could propose either approach.

A provisional plan helps people coordinate, but assumptions need to be marked. Keeping options open is useful only if someone knows when the decision will be made. Either person can check the facts and set a follow-up date.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: why their stacks differ when one letter changes

Both types have E, so the outward-facing function is dominant. In ESTJ, J points to a judging function and T identifies it as extraverted Thinking (Te), supported by introverted Sensing (Si). In ESTP, P points to a perceiving function and S identifies it as extraverted Sensing (Se), supported by introverted Thinking (Ti).

The two sets of abbreviations are different under the convention shown. Both still contain Sensing and Thinking, in different orientations and positions. A function’s place in the model does not determine when someone will take a particular step.

The Foundation lists Intuition (Ne or Ni) as the tertiary function for ESTJ and Feeling (Fe or Fi) for ESTP. This article uses Ne and Fe. Using Ni for ESTJ or Fi for ESTP would create overlap with the other type’s inferior function. See the [ESTJ profile](/en/personality/estj) and the [ESTP profile](/en/personality/estp) for their four preferences.
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
The following fictional scenes illustrate how people could make arrangements. Assign real responsibilities according to skill, authority, information and availability.

A team can agree on who will follow up and still leave the choice of remedy open. Clarify which decisions are settled and which depend on further information.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: documenting an issue found during an inspection

In a fictional store inspection, two employees find a refrigerated display outside the store’s accepted range. Both follow the same food-safety procedure and notify the responsible person. The comparison concerns the later follow-up rather than the immediate handling of the issue.

Both colleagues have the same record and deadline for a proposed follow-up. They can set a provisional review plan with an owner, or keep several follow-up options open until the authorised person assesses the findings.

They can also agree on an owner and deadline while leaving the remedy open. Either person can suggest that combination.

Record who made each observation, where the information came from and when each step took place. If a fact is missing, leave it marked as unknown. A detailed record cannot establish who visited first or what their type is.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: handling a queue during the lunch rush

In a fictional lunch rush, three delivery orders are running late. Both shift leads see the same queue and have the same staff and authority to change assignments within the store’s procedures.

One option is to set a provisional packing and handover arrangement for the rest of the rush. Another is to keep two feasible assignments available until the next check on the queue. Both approaches need clear ownership for orders already in progress.

Review what reduced the backlog and tell the next shift what changed. That evaluates the arrangement. It does not identify either shift lead’s type.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: agreeing on a relative’s temporary stay

In a fictional household, a relative asks whether their child can stay while starting university. Both household members have the same information about the proposed dates and what the home can accommodate.

Everyone affected might agree on a provisional arrangement for the whole stay or set essential terms and keep some details open for review. Neither option assumes consent from people who have not agreed.

Name what everyone needs to agree before the stay, such as the dates and access to the home. Decide what can be reviewed later, such as how chores are shared. Either person can raise both points.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
An organised desk or careful filing can reflect habit or a requirement of the job. J/P describes a preference for structure or openness in the outside world.

Either type can speak plainly or gently. The shared Thinking preference concerns what carries weight in a judgment, so tone does not establish it.

Supervising staff and adapting to changing conditions both require skills. Neither type has exclusive claim to either skill.

Opening a follow-up record or inspecting a shelf first may reflect the assignment, deadline or information on hand. The order alone does not distinguish ESTJ from ESTP.

faq_blocks.answer:
They share E, S and T but differ on J/P. ESTJ favours structure and closure in the outside world. ESTP favours keeping options open to information.

Both can plan, observe and adjust. When they make a decision can depend on the assignment, authority and what they already know.
faq_blocks.question: ### What is the main difference between ESTJ and ESTP?

faq_blocks.answer:
For both types, E puts the outward-facing process in the dominant position. J makes that process a judging function for ESTJ (Te). P makes it a perceiving function for ESTP (Se). ESTJ has auxiliary Si and ESTP has auxiliary Ti.

The stacks shown use Ne in ESTJ’s third position and Fe in ESTP’s. The Foundation lists alternative orientations. The functions describe a model and do not fix the order of someone’s actions.
faq_blocks.question: ### Why do ESTJ and ESTP have different cognitive functions?

faq_blocks.answer:
Yes. Both can follow a policy and revise a plan as new information arrives. J/P concerns the preference for structure or openness in the outside world.

Look at what the role requires and what choices the person has. One example, or a record of which step came first, cannot establish the preference.
faq_blocks.question: ### Can an ESTP follow a procedure and an ESTJ work flexibly?

faq_blocks.answer:
Yes. Competence depends on experience, training and what the job requires.

To explore the work, try reviewing a fictional inspection report, identifying what needs follow-up and writing down who owns it. Compare the exercise with the duties in a real store operations role.
faq_blocks.question: ### Can either type supervise a store?

faq_blocks.answer:
Separate what the team knows from what it still needs to verify. Agree who owns the follow-up and when the decision is due.

Follow any safety or policy requirements that apply before choosing a discretionary plan. Either person can propose a provisional arrangement or ask to keep feasible options open.
faq_blocks.question: ### How can ESTJ and ESTP agree on a follow-up plan?

faq_blocks.answer:
Compare the versions, languages and scoring. Think about which situations you used when answering questions about planning and openness.

If the tool explains its J/P score and cutoff, use that guidance. Four-letter results alone cannot show whether either score was close to the cutoff.

Under the convention used here, ESTJ is Te–Si–Ne–Fi and ESTP is Se–Ti–Fe–Ni. Both are extraverted, so their outward functions are dominant. Their auxiliary functions face inward: Si for ESTJ and Ti for ESTP. The Myers & Briggs Foundation lists alternative orientations for the tertiary functions.

Either person can collect evidence, make a plan or revise it. The role, deadline and available information help explain which step they take first. One action cannot identify a type.

sections.body_md:
ESTJ and ESTP share Extraversion (E), Sensing (S) and Thinking (T). They differ only on Judging and Perceiving (J/P). ESTJ’s J favours structure and closure in the outside world. ESTP’s P favours keeping options open to new information.

- **Shared E.** Extraversion describes a preference for directing attention and energy outward. Either type can listen quietly or speak at length.
- **Shared S.** Sensing emphasises concrete details and experience when taking in information. Both can examine the same shelf and consult the same records.
- **Shared T.** Thinking emphasises logical consistency and criteria that apply across cases. Either type can use those criteria and consider how a decision affects people.
- **The J/P difference.** In type dynamics, J points to an outward-facing judging function, Te for ESTJ. P points to an outward-facing perceiving function, Se for ESTP.

Under the convention used here, ESTJ is Te–Si–Ne–Fi and ESTP is Se–Ti–Fe–Ni. Both are extraverted, so their outward functions are dominant. Their auxiliary functions face inward: Si for ESTJ and Ti for ESTP. The Myers & Briggs Foundation lists alternative orientations for the tertiary functions.

Either person can collect evidence, make a plan or revise it. The role, deadline and available information help explain which step they take first. One action cannot identify a type.
sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
Imagine two managers who use the same checklist to ask that an open issue be resolved. Their training and responsibility may explain that similarity. How directly either person speaks gives little evidence about J/P.

The shared E, S and T concern attention, information and judgment, respectively. J/P concerns structure and openness in the outside world. Two colleagues can agree on what the facts show and still prefer to settle different parts of the plan.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: how much to settle during a store inspection

In a fictional store inspection, two colleagues find gaps on a display and receive the same stock and delivery records. They have the same authority and deadline to propose a follow-up. Both can check why shelves were not replenished.

The team could agree on a provisional plan and revise it after confirming the cause. Or it could keep several feasible plans open until the same review point. That contrast illustrates J/P. Either colleague could propose either approach.

A provisional plan helps people coordinate, but assumptions need to be marked. Keeping options open is useful only if someone knows when the decision will be made. Either person can check the facts and set a follow-up date.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: why their stacks differ when one letter changes

Both types have E, so the outward-facing function is dominant. In ESTJ, J points to a judging function and T identifies it as extraverted Thinking (Te), supported by introverted Sensing (Si). In ESTP, P points to a perceiving function and S identifies it as extraverted Sensing (Se), supported by introverted Thinking (Ti).

The two sets of abbreviations are different under the convention shown. Both still contain Sensing and Thinking, in different orientations and positions. A function’s place in the model does not determine when someone will take a particular step.

The Foundation lists Intuition (Ne or Ni) as the tertiary function for ESTJ and Feeling (Fe or Fi) for ESTP. This article uses Ne and Fe. Using Ni for ESTJ or Fi for ESTP would create overlap with the other type’s inferior function. See the [ESTJ profile](/en/personality/estj) and the [ESTP profile](/en/personality/estp) for their four preferences.
sections.title: ESTJ and ESTP: shared ground and the core difference

sections.body_md:
Each row is a fictional example. Both colleagues have the same facts, authority, procedure and deadline within that situation.

Most rows illustrate how much to settle or keep open. Either person can use the approach in either column. These are examples of the preference framework and cannot identify anyone’s type.

| Shared situation | ESTJ: possible emphasis | ESTP: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both find the same misplaced price label | Agree on a provisional plan to prevent it recurring | Keep more than one prevention plan open until the same review | J/P: provisional closure or keeping options open. Both follow the same pricing policy. |
| Both face the same staffing shortage | Set a provisional staffing plan within the same shift limits | Keep two feasible staffing plans open until the same review point | J/P: how much to settle in advance |
| Both review the same recurring issue | Compare the documented dates and circumstances of each occurrence | Compare the same dates and circumstances | Shared S: concrete information and prior experience |
| Both receive the same objection to a proposed plan | Set a provisional plan subject to review of the objection | Keep both feasible plans open until the same review | J/P: structure or openness within the same deadline |
| Both prepare the same inspection report | Agree on a provisional outline and revise it when the remaining facts arrive | Keep several workable outlines open until the same facts arrive | J/P: how much structure to give the work before review |
| Both need a schedule that meets the same new policy | Set a provisional compliant schedule | Keep more than one compliant schedule open until the same decision point | J/P: closure or flexibility. Both follow the policy. |

Someone may open a record because the procedure requires it, or wait because approval is pending. Neither the order of those actions nor report quality can establish a type.
sections.title: ESTJ and ESTP in one minute

sections.body_md:
The following fictional scenes illustrate how people could make arrangements. Assign real responsibilities according to skill, authority, information and availability.

A team can agree on who will follow up and still leave the choice of remedy open. Clarify which decisions are settled and which depend on further information.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: documenting an issue found during an inspection

In a fictional store inspection, two employees find a refrigerated display outside the store’s accepted range. Both follow the same food-safety procedure and notify the responsible person. The comparison concerns the later follow-up rather than the immediate handling of the issue.

Both colleagues have the same record and deadline for a proposed follow-up. They can set a provisional review plan with an owner, or keep several follow-up options open until the authorised person assesses the findings.

They can also agree on an owner and deadline while leaving the remedy open. Either person can suggest that combination.

Record who made each observation, where the information came from and when each step took place. If a fact is missing, leave it marked as unknown. A detailed record cannot establish who visited first or what their type is.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: handling a queue during the lunch rush

In a fictional lunch rush, three delivery orders are running late. Both shift leads see the same queue and have the same staff and authority to change assignments within the store’s procedures.

One option is to set a provisional packing and handover arrangement for the rest of the rush. Another is to keep two feasible assignments available until the next check on the queue. Both approaches need clear ownership for orders already in progress.

Review what reduced the backlog and tell the next shift what changed. That evaluates the arrangement. It does not identify either shift lead’s type.

### ### ESTJ and ESTP: agreeing on a relative’s temporary stay

In a fictional household, a relative asks whether their child can stay while starting university. Both household members have the same information about the proposed dates and what the home can accommodate.

Everyone affected might agree on a provisional arrangement for the whole stay or set essential terms and keep some details open for review. Neither option assumes consent from people who have not agreed.

Name what everyone needs to agree before the stay, such as the dates and access to the home. Decide what can be reviewed later, such as how chores are shared. Either person can raise both points.
sections.title: ESTJ and ESTP at work and in relationships

sections.body_md:
An organised desk or careful filing can reflect habit or a requirement of the job. J/P describes a preference for structure or openness in the outside world.

Either type can speak plainly or gently. The shared Thinking preference concerns what carries weight in a judgment, so tone does not establish it.

Supervising staff and adapting to changing conditions both require skills. Neither type has exclusive claim to either skill.

Opening a follow-up record or inspecting a shelf first may reflect the assignment, deadline or information on hand. The order alone does not distinguish ESTJ from ESTP.
sections.title: ESTJ and ESTP: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
If your results differ, compare the instruments, versions, languages and scoring. Consider whether you answered with similar situations in mind and how much choice you had in them.

Choose several comparable situations. Note which arrangements you settled, which options you kept open and what the role or deadline required. Include occasions when you did something different.

The notes can help you describe what you prefer when you have a choice. They cannot assign a type or validate a test result.
sections.title: ESTJ and ESTP: how to keep observing

items.answer:
They share E, S and T but differ on J/P. ESTJ favours structure and closure in the outside world. ESTP favours keeping options open to information.

Both can plan, observe and adjust. When they make a decision can depend on the assignment, authority and what they already know.
items.question: ### What is the main difference between ESTJ and ESTP?

items.answer:
For both types, E puts the outward-facing process in the dominant position. J makes that process a judging function for ESTJ (Te). P makes it a perceiving function for ESTP (Se). ESTJ has auxiliary Si and ESTP has auxiliary Ti.

The stacks shown use Ne in ESTJ’s third position and Fe in ESTP’s. The Foundation lists alternative orientations. The functions describe a model and do not fix the order of someone’s actions.
items.question: ### Why do ESTJ and ESTP have different cognitive functions?

items.answer:
Yes. Both can follow a policy and revise a plan as new information arrives. J/P concerns the preference for structure or openness in the outside world.

Look at what the role requires and what choices the person has. One example, or a record of which step came first, cannot establish the preference.
items.question: ### Can an ESTP follow a procedure and an ESTJ work flexibly?

items.answer:
Yes. Competence depends on experience, training and what the job requires.

To explore the work, try reviewing a fictional inspection report, identifying what needs follow-up and writing down who owns it. Compare the exercise with the duties in a real store operations role.
items.question: ### Can either type supervise a store?

items.answer:
Separate what the team knows from what it still needs to verify. Agree who owns the follow-up and when the decision is due.

Follow any safety or policy requirements that apply before choosing a discretionary plan. Either person can propose a provisional arrangement or ask to keep feasible options open.
items.question: ### How can ESTJ and ESTP agree on a follow-up plan?

items.answer:
Compare the versions, languages and scoring. Think about which situations you used when answering questions about planning and openness.

If the tool explains its J/P score and cutoff, use that guidance. Four-letter results alone cannot show whether either score was close to the cutoff.

sections.title: ESTJ and ESTP: common questions

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** The [Myers-Briggs official facts page](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts) explains the preferences. The Foundation’s [type dynamics explanation](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) and [type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/) give the function positions and tertiary alternatives.

**Function notation.** This article uses Te–Si–Ne–Fi for ESTJ and Se–Ti–Fe–Ni for ESTP. The Foundation also lists Ni for ESTJ’s tertiary Intuition and Fi for ESTP’s tertiary Feeling.

**Fictional examples.** The store inspection, lunch rush and temporary stay are invented. They illustrate decision-making under shared conditions and cannot establish anyone’s type.

**Scope.** Four-letter preference descriptions cannot rank ability, screen applicants or predict relationships. Interpret a result in the context of the questionnaire and the circumstances in which you answered.

FermatMind Editorial
